name: Polyperchon's regency
alt: Party of the kings (Polyperchon and Olympias)

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
predecessors.text: Macedon and Thessaly, the regent's seat of government in 319-317

successors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
successors.text: Macedon, held by Cassander after Pydna fell 'in the spring of 316'

successors.name: Antigonid kingdom (Macedon)
successors.text: Polyperchon's Peloponnesian cities, taken by Demetrius in 303: 'Demetrius Poliorcetes launched a campaign in Greece and quickly reversed many of Polyperchon's gains'

ledger.x: 319: 'In 319 BC, shortly before his death, the aging Antipater appointed Polyperchon as regent' and made Cassander chiliarch; Cassander refused the arrangement and the civil war began.
317: 'Waging war on Polyperchon, Cassander destroyed his fleet' and 'declared himself Regent in 317 BC'; 'he suffered a major setback at Megalopolis in 317 BC'.
Spring 316: 'When the city fell in the spring of 316, Olympias was killed'.
316: Polyperchon driven from Macedon to the Peloponnese after Olympias's death.

309: 'Cassander bribed Polyperchon to kill the boy [Heracles], promising him an alliance and the return of his Macedonian estates'; 'Polyperchon murdered the boy in 309 BC' and was recognised as Cassander's strategos of the Peloponnese.
303: the Peloponnesian cities fall to Demetrius; Polyperchon's command lapses.
303: 'In 303 BC, Demetrius Poliorcetes launched a campaign in Greece and quickly reversed many of Polyperchon's gains'.
303: Polyperchon is 'last heard of' after Demetrius's campaign; his death date is unknown.

wars.name: Second War of the Diadochi (Polyperchon and Olympias against Cassander)
wars.outcome: Cassander's victory: Olympias killed at Pydna (spring 316), Polyperchon driven to the Peloponnese; Aeacides of Epirus, Olympias's ally, 'was dethroned in 313 BC'.

wars.name: Demetrius's Greek campaign of 303
wars.outcome: Demetrius 'quickly reversed many of Polyperchon's gains' and revived the League of Corinth (302).

certainty.note: A faction, not a bounded state: who held which district of Macedon in 318-316 shifted with the armies.
The Peloponnesian cities are unnamed on the pages; the envelope is an outer limit at confidence 1.
